static_traits.name: Lin Jia
static_traits.social_status: Has support resources of roommates and classmates, but finds it hard to open up about financial problems; anxiety and irritability cause strained relationships with roommates and classmates
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical disease; has not previously received psychological counseling; no history of similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe stress and anxiety; attitude rather negative, often uses catastrophizing and 'never able to' statements; skeptical about exploration but willing to try, with a cooperative attitude

basic_info.main_problem: After an unexpected car tire replacement increased my expenses, I worry I cannot save enough for a class trip to Japan; I persistently feel stress, anxiety, and despair, which intensifies as the trip approaches; anxiety and hopelessness recur whenever I think about the trip or finances, especially after unexpected expenses.
basic_info.core_demands: Because stress and anxiety related to travel and finances have begun to affect academic performance and overall physical and mental state, the client hopes to relieve anxiety through counseling and restore academic and life functioning.

core_beliefs: No matter how hard I try, things will go wrong

special_situations.event: Unexpectedly needing to replace the car tires with new ones, increasing expenses
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once an unexpected expense occurs, I will not be able to achieve the set plan (such as travel savings)
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately budgeting strictly and cutting expenses in an attempt to regain control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Now it is impossible for me to save enough money for the trip to Japan

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking about the trip to Japan or one's own financial situation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot save money exactly as planned, it equals complete failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids talking about money with others; reduces social contact

special_situations.event: When interacting with roommates or classmates, topics of travel or money come up
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not share the same anxiety as me, it means they do not understand and may even judge me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Becomes irritable, keeps distance from people, or avoids conversation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No one understands how serious this matter is to me

special_situations.event: Still feels stressed after having made a budget and cut expenses
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only when there are no obstacles does effort count as effective; once a problem appears, all effort is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Disqualifying small progress already made; persistent worry and self-negation

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and supported, to seek help safely, and to maintain a sense of control over life and finances
core_conflict.fear: Fears being judged or feeling shame for exposing financial difficulties; fears losing control and plans falling through
defense_goal: Reducing shame by avoiding talking about money and seeking help
Attributes stress to external factors (such as 'the universe is against me') to relieve self-blame
Maintaining distance with reasons such as 'too personal, too embarrassing', reducing the risk of exposure

object_relations.object_representation: Others who do not understand and may judge oneself (roommates, classmates)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites the client to explore strong automatic thoughts or suggests discussing financial troubles with others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes discussion will only expose their shame, and others will not understand or will judge them (transference: worrying about being rejected / humiliated)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathize with their embarrassment and worry, with a gentle tone, provide small and safe options to try, avoid directly forcing self-disclosure, and use open-ended questions and concretizing guidance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When unexpected expenses arise or a trip approaches, triggering intense anxiety
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Blames the predicament on external factors (such as 'the universe is against me') and assumes others will not understand them
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintains a stable and accepting tone, conducts gentle reality testing, helps distinguish facts from inferences, and guides identification and naming of one's own feelings and needs.

manifestations: Feeling that 'all efforts are in vain'
Viewing one unexpected expense as the collapse of the entire plan
Interpreting the future with negative inevitability
outcomes: Decreased academic attention and slipping grades

manifestations: Finding it hard to talk to roommates and classmates about financial troubles, feeling it is too personal and too embarrassing
Experiencing 'no one understands how serious this is for me'

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward others or the outside world, gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self (turning the energy toward the self).
manifestations: Does not seek help from roommates or classmates, instead imposing stricter self-frugality and self-pressure
Pushing back the impulse to seek help and bearing anxiety and worry alone

contact_model.definition: Attributing feelings one cannot accept to others or the outside world.
manifestations: Attributing the predicament to 'the universe is against me'
Believing others will not understand or will judge oneself

contact_model.definition: Has poor self-reflection and introspection, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Does not talk about money for fear of embarrassment; cares excessively about others' opinions
Highly cautious about self-disclosure; would rather avoid communication

positive_force: Has proactively tried budgeting and cutting expenses
Has potential social support resources (roommates, classmates)
In counseling, willing to try small steps and decatastrophizing exercises
Clear goal (going to Japan with the class), motivation present
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, all-or-nothing thinking, and jumping to conclusions
Ashamed to talk about money and avoids seeking help, making resources hard to mobilize
Anxiety and irritability disrupt sleep and eating and strain interpersonal relationships
Tends to regard the outside world as hostile ('the universe is against me'), and self-efficacy decreases

target_behavior.behavior: 回避与他人讨论财务困扰
antecedent: Thinking about the cost of the Japan trip with the class
Unexpected expenses arising (such as replacing a tire)
Social occasions involve travel or money topics
target_behavior.core_reason: Feels embarrassed about money topics, fears being judged or not understood, and thus avoids disclosure and seeking help
target_behavior.function: Escaping shame and negative evaluation, maintaining self-protection and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Support resources are unavailable, interpersonal relationships are tense and estranged, aggravating anxiety and powerlessness

target_behavior.behavior: Interprets financial stress catastrophically and falls into intense anxiety, accompanied by irritability and reduced attention to study
antecedent: 独自思考旅行与财务时
target_behavior.core_reason: Makes negative predictions and all-or-nothing attributions about the future, excessively magnifying the impact of a single event
target_behavior.function: Tries to gain a false sense of control and psychological preparedness by anticipating the worst scenario, avoiding in the short term the anxiety brought by uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired academic performance, disturbed sleep and eating rhythms, increased interpersonal conflict
